title: Alibaba, Solaria in Talks for Spanish Data Center Power Supply
source_used: briefs.co (a rewrite of the Bloomberg report); Bloomberg itself blocked
key_facts: Bloomberg reports, citing unnamed people with knowledge of the talks, that Alibaba Group has held early talks with Solaria Energia y Medio Ambiente about supplying renewable power to a potential data center in Spain.
The Solaria site under review is in Puertollano, about 240 kilometers south of Madrid.
One person said the idea is less advanced than the European data centers Alibaba has already said it will build, and that Alibaba has also sounded out other power providers.
Spokespeople for both companies declined to comment.
Alibaba said the week before that it will open its first cloud hubs in Finland and the Netherlands within a year and expand data center operations in Germany and France.

Spain is preparing rules, aimed for year end, that would require data centers in Spain to be run by EU-based companies, keep operational data in the EU, and match extra power demand with newly built clean energy.
quote_evidence: Alibaba has held early talks with Solaria about sourcing renewable electricity for a potential data center in Spain, according to people familiar.
Spokespeople for both companies declined to comment.
why_it_matters_hint: A Chinese cloud company is scouting clean power in Spain as Europe's data center rules take shape, but the talks are early and unconfirmed.
notes: Bloomberg returned HTTP 403 (bot check). The facts above come from briefs.co, a site that rewrites Bloomberg's report, plus a partial Yahoo Finance (MT Newswires) snippet that also says 'preliminary talks'; neither is Bloomberg's own text, so treat details as unconfirmed by us. Investing.com, qz.com and MarketScreener were also blocked.
